watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier — refusal count, kill-exit count, and the firings denominator they are counted against
watchme.nexus: /intent's trace berth plus the verdict corpus in CairnCommons/learning/ — the same store the parent's akien-gate-dial reads, at a narrower scope
watchme.consumer: Akien. Distinct from the parent's watch on purpose: akien-gate-dial asks 'can this gate be DELEGATED yet' across the roster; this one asks 'does link 1's door ever actually RED' — the vacuity question, which is falsifier (4) and cannot be answered by the parent's dial.

falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) /intent fires and leaves no trace — GREENS INCLUDED; the unrecorded green destroys the denominator; (2) /intent reaches either exit without emitting a bullet-list finding, or emits bullets no gate ever sees; (3) the anatomy is prose in SKILL.md rather than a call into the primitive — discipline wearing physics' clothes, inherited from the parent's falsifier (5); (4) the door never REDS across the first measurement window while inputs are demonstrably imperfect — a gate that cannot refuse is vacuous (the coin-toss-green lesson), and this is the watch's own question; (5) THE TEMPLATE CLAIM FAILS — migrating skill #2 cannot copy the pattern without redesign, meaning child b produced a one-off and not the template brick it is chartered as; (6) a ticket reaches BUILDME carrying no /intent berth and the gate lets it through — the ruling of 2026-08-01 unimplemented while the ticket claims done.
horizon: Re-read when skill #2 (/challenge, child c) migrates — that is when the template claim (falsifier 5) is first measurable rather than asserted. The watch's own horizon is the first window in which /intent fires on real work.
distinctions_recorded: TWO DIALS, NOT A DUPLICATION. chart's dial measures WHICH STRATUM ANSWERED (floor/tree/claude — a COMPILATION metric: is the boundary moving down). learning_block's dial measures AKIEN'S GATE BEHAVIOUR (firings, send_backs, approvals, match_rate — a DELEGATION metric: can this gate be handed off). Different axes, neither terminal. Measured this session: cairn/chart/ contains zero references to learning_block.

TWO STORES, DIFFERENT OBJECTS. chart trees hold CONTENT (what was decided about this class of request); learning traces hold BEHAVIOUR (did the door refuse, did the gate approve). This is NOT a second write path into CairnCommons/learning/ — learning_block's falsifier (7) is not tripped.

'/intent DOESN'T FILE TO COMMONS' IS NOT VIOLATED. That rule exists so an UNRESOLVED NODE is not filed as though resolved. A verdict record is not the node — it is the record of the firing. Recorded explicitly because it reads as a contradiction at a glance and a future reader will trip on it.

A SKILL'S DOOR CANNOT BE PHYSICS BY BEING CALLED. The executor of a skill is an LLM reading markdown, so a door the markdown ASKS to be called can be skipped or fed a shaped payload — the exact skate the parent ticket exists to close. Cairn already solved this for LLM-executed steps and NOT by trust: (a) the stage gate refuses a malformed packet, (b) the next stage template-fills from the previous berth so skipping is a build error, (c) a downstream consumer refuses to proceed without the artifact (the emit chokepoint's EntryGateRed). This ticket APPLIES that proven pattern rather than inventing skill-migration machinery — which is also what makes 'template brick' a strong claim: the pattern has already survived nine instances.

THE MOST VALUABLE FIRING IS THE ONE THAT VANISHES TODAY. /intent has TWO exits: routed-forward, and routed-OUT (nothing traces to the Telos, so the node dies here). The kill is the cheapest win in the system — an intention that shouldn't exist, stopped before any cost — and it is the one exit with NO downstream artifact to record it. It currently vanishes into conversation. This single case justifies the trace organ better than any argument brought into the pass; it is why 'finding at BOTH exits' is in the intention and not an afterthought.

THE SKILLS ARE IN GIT. Measured this session: ~/.claude/skills/* are SYMLINKS into skills/<name>/ (same inode). A skill is therefore a proper code-seam-shaped node with one code address that can carry state/history beside it (skills/sail/ already does) — NOT a host-seam whose implementation git cannot see. This is what makes the class assignment 'skill' rather than 'host-seam' a measured call.

THIS TICKET CANNOT CARRY THE BERTH IT MANDATES. /intent was fired on this very node (dogfooding: the first act of migrating /intent is firing it), but the berth mechanism is what this ticket BUILDS — so the firing exists in conversation only. The chicken-and-egg is named here rather than papered over; the gate's first real subject is the ticket AFTER this one.
open_design_questions_for_the_chart_chai: WHERE THE GATE SITS. Akien's ruling is 'no cast without /intent'. Two candidate seats: (a) the ticket carries an `intent_berth` field and the EXISTING BUILDME entry gate — already refusing a missing chart claim — refuses a missing berth too (cheapest, proven, no new door; a cast without /intent produces a ticket that cannot be built, which is the ruling in effect); (b) a `cairn cast` door becomes the SOLE writer into CairnCommons/tickets/, the record_verdict pattern applied to casting (stronger, literal, and a larger build). CC's lean is (a); decompose settles it with the bounds in front of it.
THE TRACE UNIT — the firing as a whole, or each of the five questions? Per-question is a finer denominator and a heavier wire.

THE SHELL REACH. Measured absence: __main__ exposes trace, dial, recordverdict and EXPLICITLY refuses finding events ('findings go through python'). No door or finding exists from bash anywhere in the system. Whether /intent needs new shell verbs or an inline python step is a build decision, not a design one — but it is the reason child b touches the primitive at all.
cost_note: /intent today costs about two tool calls (the recompile-gate poke and the congruency-lab read). Door plus finding roughly DOUBLES its step count. The charter calls it 'the cheapest gate in the system', so the honest number belongs here rather than the word 'cheap': still trivial against a wasted voyage, and that ratio — not the absolute cost — is what the claim rests on.
